name: Montana
standard: WCAG 2.1 AA (per SITSD guidance / ADA Title II); statutory nonvisual access standard for procurement

laws.summary: IT procured by state agencies must give blind and visually impaired users equivalent access, and every state IT contract must include a technology access clause set by the Department of Administration.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

applies_to: State agencies (MCA 18-5 Part 6 for IT procurement); SITSD guidance for state websites and apps; local governments via ADA Title II only.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Technology access clause in all state IT contracts (statute)
Agency head ensures procured IT supports nonvisual access
Undue-burden exemption by good-faith agency determination
SITSD guidance: design, test and author to WCAG 2.1 AA; no formal coordinator or statement mandate found
mobile: implied — SITSD guidance says ADA Title II covers web content and mobile apps; statute is technology-neutral.
procurement: Mandatory technology access clause (MCA 18-5-604) with nonvisual access standards developed by the Department of Administration; agency heads may not exclude it for OS/software compatibility or new system design.
enforcement: No state enforcement body or penalty identified beyond procurement conditions; ADA Title II complaints.
notes: No formal Montana enterprise accessibility policy/standard document found; the 'State of Montana Accessibility Policy' link on SITSD points to a general mt.gov disclaimer page (not reviewed). sitsd.mt.gov/Accessibility/Standards returned 404. The text of the technology access clause itself was not located.
